import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

np.random.seed(42)
population = np.random.exponential(1, size=100000)

pop_mean = np.mean(population)
pop_std = np.std(population)

n = 30
n_samples = 10000
sample_means = np.mean(np.random.exponential(1, size=(n_samples, n)), axis=1)

mean_of_means = np.mean(sample_means)
std_of_means = np.std(sample_means)

expected_std = pop_std / np.sqrt(n)

ks_stat, ks_pvalue = stats.kstest(sample_means, 'norm', args=(mean_of_means, std_of_means))

for sample_n in [5, 10, 30, 100]:
    means = np.mean(np.random.exponential(1, size=(n_samples, sample_n)), axis=1)
    ks_stat_n, _ = stats.kstest(means, 'norm', args=(np.mean(means), np.std(means)))
    print(f"n={sample_n}: KS statistic = {ks_stat_n:.4f}")

theoretical_quantiles = stats.norm.ppf(np.linspace(0.01, 0.99, 100))
sample_quantiles = np.quantile(sample_means, np.linspace(0.01, 0.99, 100))

print(f"Population mean: {pop_mean:.4f}, std: {pop_std:.4f}")
print(f"Mean of sample means: {mean_of_means:.4f}")
print(f"Std of sample means: {std_of_means:.4f}")
print(f"Expected std (pop/sqrt(n)): {expected_std:.4f}")
print(f"KS test statistic: {ks_stat:.4f}, p-value: {ks_pvalue:.4f}")
